question: What is a Tax Waiver under URA and what is the Tujenge Pack?
answer: A tax waiver is a statutory relief from paying tax, penalties, or interest for a specific period administered by URA under the Tax Procedures Code Act (TPCA). Under the URA Tujenge Pack initiative published at https://ura.go.ug/en/tujenge-pack/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/tax-waiver/ (published March 29, 2026 and February 3, 2026 by Daisy Namakula, with official brochure at https://ura.go.ug/download-category/tax-waiver-brochure/), Government provides taxpayers relief to promote voluntary compliance, alleviate financial hardship, and resolve disputes without costly litigation. A tax waiver reduces or eliminates accrued tax liability without changing future tax obligations.

question: What are the legal provisions and eligibility rules for the 100% Tax Waiver under Section 47B of the TPCA?
answer: The tax waiver is provided for under Section 47B of the Tax Procedures Code Act (TPCA) (and previously under Sections 47A, 47, and 46 of the TPCA). Under Section 47B: 1) A taxpayer benefits from a 100% waiver of penal tax and interest outstanding as at 30th June 2024 where the taxpayer pays all of the principal tax by 30th June 2026; 2) Where a taxpayer pays part of their principal tax outstanding as at 30th June 2024 by 30th June 2026, interest and penalties are waived on a pro-rata basis (to the extent of the principal tax paid); 3) Interest and penalty charged on outstanding principal tax after 30th June 2024 is covered under this waiver.

question: Which taxes are covered under the URA Tax Waiver?
answer: The tax waiver covers penalties and interest accrued under Uganda Domestic Tax Laws: 1) Income Tax Act (Cap. 340); 2) Value Added Tax Act (Cap. 349); 3) Excise Duty Act 2014; 4) Lotteries and Gaming Act 2016; and 5) Stamp Duty Act 2014. The waiver applies automatically once the taxpayer meets the statutory conditions by settling principal tax by 30th June 2026.

question: What penalties and liabilities are excluded from the Section 47B Tax Waiver?
answer: Under Section 47B TPCA and the Tax Waiver Brochure FY 2025/26, the waiver does NOT cover: 1) Interest and penalties relating to principal tax for periods whose due date is after 30th June 2024; 2) Penal tax for failure to provide information; 3) Penal tax in relation to Digital Tax Stamps (DTS); 4) Penal tax in relation to non-compliance with EFRIS electronic invoicing; 5) Penalty for failing to apply for tax registration; and 6) Court-imposed penalties and interest.

question: Where can I download the official URA Tax Waiver Brochure and what is its scope?
answer: The official Tax Waiver Brochure FY 2025/26 is published and downloadable from the URA Tax Education Archives at https://ura.go.ug/download-category/tax-waiver-brochure/ (package ID 67672, 898 KB PDF, 149+ downloads). It details the operational guidelines for the Section 47B TPCA waiver, pro-rata relief calculations, domestic tax eligibility, and non-waivable statutory penalties.

question: How does the pro-rata tax waiver calculation work under Section 47B TPCA?
answer: Under Section 47B of the Tax Procedures Code Act, if a taxpayer owes outstanding principal tax as at 30th June 2024 but can only pay a portion of it before 30th June 2026, the accumulated penal tax and interest are waived in direct proportion to the principal paid. For example, if a taxpayer with UGX 10,000,000 principal tax and UGX 6,000,000 penalty/interest pays UGX 5,000,000 (50%) of principal by 30th June 2026, exactly 50% (UGX 3,000,000) of the penalty and interest is permanently waived, leaving the remaining balance subject to normal enforcement.
